description: Set WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.08 and give the per-layer scalar AdamW groups (resid and x0 lambdas) a separate weight decay of 1e-4 times the matrix value.
Enable a short linear LR warmup over the first 5% of the time budget by setting WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.05, using the existing schedule code.
Split Muon groups by layer parity, using 0.95*MATRIX_LR for even layers and 0.85*MATRIX_LR for odd layers.
Add LRSCHEDULES giving Muon layers 0-4 0.4*MATRIX_LR and layers 5+ 0.8*MATRIX_LR by splitting Muon groups per (shape, layer ratio).
Initialize resid_lambdas to 1.3 instead of 1.0 so each layer computes 1.3*residual + x0 mix.
No change: the stop-loss idea is ill-defined here and either always triggers or never does.
No change: the min-loss penalty would never trigger in this setting.

issues: Integrity check passed: the diff only changes get_lr_multiplier. It does not touch the evaluation call, the val_bpb measurement, the data, the prepare.py import line or the seed lines. There is no reason to veto.

No bug that makes the result meaningless: the new schedule is valid code. It assumes progress = elapsed training time / TIME_BUDGET, which matches the time-based loop, and that TIME_BUDGET (300 s) is at least 100 s, which it is. The run measures what it is meant to measure.

This is a poor schedule rather than a broken one. It drops warmup and starts at the full LR. It then decays linearly to 0.1x over the first 60 s, holds 0.1x for about 200 s, and decays to 0.01x over the last 40 s. Running most of training at 10% LR fits the clear regression: 1.2471 against the incumbent's 1.1145, about 0.13 bpb worse.
Leftover code: WARMUP_RATIO, WARMDOWN_RATIO and FINAL_LR_FRAC are no longer used by the schedule, and the 60/40/0.1/0.01 constants are hardcoded. This would matter only if the candidate were kept.

On the numbers: z cannot be fully recomputed because the incumbent's standard deviation is not given. With n=1 for the candidate, z = (1.1145 - 1.2471)/s = -23.494 implies s ≈ 0.00564, a plausible run-to-run spread. The sign (candidate worse) matches the reject decision.
There are no claims that contradict the harness numbers. The provisional reject is correct.

description: Replace the progress-based warmdown LR schedule with a clock-based one: 1.0 to 0.1 linearly over the first 60s, flat at 0.1 until 260s, then a linear sink to 0.01 at the end of the budget.
Apply training-only dropout to the MLP hidden activations, with a drop rate that varies sinusoidally with sequence position (0 to 0.1, period 256).
Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2^18 (divisor p=2 of 2^19) so the fixed 300 s budget yields about twice as many optimizer steps.
No change: the spec is self-contradictory and adds complexity for no clear gain.
Add a training-only penalty of 4.1e-6 times the mean per-token sum of squared residual activations after the first three layers to the loss.
Replace the flat-then-linear warmdown LR multiplier with a logistic sigmoid of training progress (center 0.65, steepness 10) applied to all optimizer groups.
No change: periodic validation is only a diagnostic and cannot lower val_bpb.

No change: DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 256 would overflow 40 GB (128 already does). It would also fail the TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE divisibility assert, because 256*2048 exceeds the 2^18 step. A larger tokens-per-step also contradicts the slot 7 result, where fewer tokens per step won.
No change: the spec doesn't fit this model, and the closest versions would hurt.
Apply a small soft-threshold (softshrink, lambda=0.02) to the residual stream before the resid/x0 mixing at each layer to suppress tiny activations.
Add stochastic depth: during the first 200s of training, each block is skipped with probability 0.2 via a buffer-controlled gate, then turned off.
No change: scaling gradients by 0.99 for layers 3-7 has no effect, because Muon's orthogonalization and NorMuon normalization remove gradient scale.
Replace each block's output with a q-residual that mixes 30% of the block input with 70% of the block output (x = 0.7*block(x) + 0.3*x).
No change: a grand batch of 256 sequences is 2^19 tokens, which undoes the accepted slot 7 win.
Soft-threshold each block's attention and MLP outputs before adding them to the residual stream, with lambda growing linearly with depth (0.02*(i+1)/n_layer).
No change: the ripple-injection spec is self-contradictory and would be mostly undone by Muon's orthogonalization.

issues: (1) No integrity problems. The diff only adds a CrossAttention module to each block, initializes its weights and passes x0 into the blocks. The evaluation call, data, seed lines, the prepare.py import and the final summary printing are not touched.

(2) No bug that makes the result meaningless. The cross-attention uses causal=True with the same window_size, and its keys and values come from x0 (the token embeddings at the same positions), so it cannot see future tokens. RoPE and QK-norm are applied the same way as in self-attention, and c_proj starts at zero, so the model starts out matching the incumbent. One thing I could not check: whether the optimizer setup picks up the new xattn weights. That depends on code outside the diff. If it collects matrix parameters from transformer.h, they are included.

(3) No claims were made beyond the harness numbers. The candidate scored 1.1011 against the incumbent's 1.0943, which is 0.0068 worse (lower val_bpb is better). That fits with each layer doing about 33% more attention work, so fewer steps fit in the fixed 300 s. Rejecting is consistent with the numbers.

z cannot be recomputed on its own: each side has only one run, so there is no variance estimate to divide by. The harness's z = -0.880 implies a noise sigma of about 0.0077 (0.0068 / 0.88). Its sign and size are plausible, but I could not verify the value.
Simplicity: about 25 extra lines and roughly 4·n_embd² more parameters per layer, with no gain. Even if the result were equal, this would not be worth keeping.

issues: Integrity check: I found no integrity problems. The diff only changes the attention forward pass. It leaves the val_bpb measurement, the data, the seed lines, the prepare.py import and the evaluation call untouched.

Correctness check: the change is causal. F.pad(q, (0,0,0,0,2,0)) adds two positions to the front of the time dimension (dim 1, assuming q is laid out as (B, T, H, D)). That makes qp[:,1:-1] equal to q[t-1] and qp[:,:-2] equal to q[t-2], so no future tokens leak in. The weights add up to 1.75, so dividing by 1.75 keeps the scale the same. The mixing happens before rotary embeddings are applied, so it isn't a bug, but it does mean neighbouring queries are blended without their position phases.

z = 0.020 can't be recomputed. There is one candidate run (1.0941) and one incumbent run (1.0943), so neither side has a variance estimate. The raw difference is 0.0002 in the candidate's favour, which is far smaller than normal run-to-run noise. The z the harness reports agrees with that, and so does its provisional reject.
Claims check: the diff makes no claims that conflict with the numbers. The one comment only describes what the code does.
Simplicity: this adds code for a gain that can't be told apart from zero. Under the simplicity rule it isn't worth keeping unless replicate runs show a real effect.

description: Causal left-only variant of temporal order mixing: replace each query with an exponentially decaying (1, 0.5, 0.25) weighted average of its own and the two previous positions' queries before rotary and QK-norm; right context is dropped because it would leak future tokens.
